official.deadline_central_display: 3 June 2026 (closing date extended from 20 May 2026; originally 6 to 20 May 2026, opening 6 March 2026)
official.deadline_note: Official wording: 'Opening date of this fellowship: 6 March 2026' and 'Closing date of this fellowship: 6 then 20 May 2026 now extended until 3 June 2026'. Applications can only be submitted to TWAS through the online portal once the call is open.
official.status_note: The TWAS opportunity page states plainly 'The call is closed'. Results of the selection are expected at the end of 2026 or early 2027, and selected candidates will be able to start their fellowship no earlier than 2027.
benefits: A monthly stipend from CSIR to cover living costs, food and health insurance
Placement in a CSIR research laboratory or institute with research facilities in emerging areas of science and technology
Up to four years of funding for full-time fellowships
Sandwich fellowships of a minimum of six months, up to a maximum decided by the host institute but no greater than three years
eligibility: Maximum age of 35 years on 31 December of the application year
National of a developing country in the South, other than India
Must not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
Hold a Master's degree in science and technology
Be regularly employed in the home country and hold a research assignment there
Sandwich fellowships: be a registered PhD student in the home country and provide the 'Registration and No Objection Certificate' from the home university
Full-time fellowships: be willing to register at a university in India within the first year, if agreed to by CSIR
Be accepted at a CSIR laboratory or institution and provide an official acceptance letter from the host institution
Provide evidence of proficiency in English if the medium of education was not English
Provide evidence that s/he will return to the home country on completion of the fellowship
Not take up other assignments during the period of the fellowship
Be financially responsible for any accompanying family members
requirements: Applications for the programme can only be submitted to TWAS via the online portal, once the call is open
Applicants may apply for only one programme per calendar year in the TWAS and OWSD portfolio

Only acceptance letters dated the same year as the year of application are eligible
Requests for acceptance must be directed to the chosen CSIR host institution(s); without preliminary acceptance the application will not be considered for selection
Applicants must apply for only one programme per calendar year, and are not eligible for a TWAS Visiting Professor programme in that year

Registration and No Objection Certificate signed by the Vice-Chancellor or Registrar of the home university, for sandwich applicants, with a copy sent to both CSIR and TWAS
Evidence of proficiency in English, if the medium of education was not English
Evidence that the applicant will return to the home country on completion of the fellowship
selection_criteria: Acceptance at a CSIR laboratory or institution, evidenced by an official acceptance letter, without which the application is not considered for selection
The field of research must fall within the emerging areas of science and technology for which facilities are available in CSIR laboratories and institutes
Eligibility of the chosen host among the CSIR laboratories and institutes listed on the programme page
Only one programme per calendar year may be applied for in the TWAS and OWSD portfolio
coverage: Monthly stipend from CSIR to cover living costs, food and health insurance
Research facilities in a CSIR laboratory or institute
application_method: Register on the TWAS online application portal at onlineforms.twas.org/apply/300 once the call is open
Request the preliminary acceptance letter from the chosen CSIR host institution as early as possible, ideally before the call opens, and ensure it is dated the same year as the application
Complete the online form and upload the supporting documents listed in the call, using the applicant tutorial and sample acceptance letter published on the page
For sandwich applicants, send a copy of the home university Registration and No Objection Certificate to both CSIR and TWAS
Await the selection result, expected at the end of 2026 or early 2027, with fellows able to start no earlier than 2027
official.application_route: Apply to TWAS through the online portal only, after first securing a preliminary acceptance letter from the chosen CSIR host laboratory or institute.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationals of developing countries in the South, other than India, who do not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country.
official.international_eligibility: The programme is open only to nationals of developing countries other than India; Indian nationals are excluded, as is anyone holding residency in India or in a developed country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Tenable only in CSIR research laboratories and institutes, across agricultural sciences; structural, cell and molecular biology; biological systems and organisms; medical and health sciences including neurosciences; chemical sciences; engineering sciences; astronomy, space and earth sciences; mathematical sciences; and physics. The chosen host must be one of the eligible CSIR laboratories and institutes.
official.research_requirement: Applicants pursue research toward a PhD in emerging areas of science and technology for which facilities are available in CSIR laboratories and institutes. Sandwich applicants must already be registered PhD students in their home country; full-time applicants must be willing to register at a university in India within the first year if agreed by CSIR.
official.duration: Full-time fellowships up to a maximum of four years; sandwich fellowships for a minimum of six months up to a maximum decided by the host institute but no greater than three years.
official.description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research of India and UNESCO-TWAS have established a number of fellowships for foreign scholars from developing countries who wish to pursue research toward a PhD in emerging areas of science and technology, for which facilities are available in CSIR laboratories and institutes. TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowships are tenable in CSIR research laboratories and institutes in India for a maximum period of four years.
official.program_type: Doctoral research fellowship tenable in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India
official.english_requirement: The language of instruction for foreign scholars in CSIR laboratories/institutes is English; applicants must provide evidence of proficiency in English if the medium of their education was not English.

applicant_utility.summary: The decisive document here is not your CV but an acceptance letter from a CSIR laboratory, and it has to be dated in the same year as your application - a letter from last year is worthless. That makes this a fellowship you secure first and apply for second, so contact prospective CSIR hosts months before a call opens. The other hard filters are unusual and unforgiving: you must be 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, hold a Master's in science and technology, be currently employed with a research assignment in your home country, and hold no residency visa for India or any developed country. TWAS does not publish what CSIR actually pays, only that the monthly stipend covers living costs, food and health insurance with subsidized accommodation, so plan your finances around an unknown figure and a start no earlier than 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Employed Master's-level scientists and engineers from developing countries, aged 35 or under, who already have a research post at home and a named CSIR host willing to take them for a PhD placement.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify candidate CSIR laboratories from the CSIR network map or the eligible-centres list published on the TWAS page, and start requesting acceptance letters months before the call opens
Confirm the acceptance letter is dated in the same calendar year as your application year
Line up the Registration and No Objection Certificate signed by your home university's Vice-Chancellor or Registrar, and plan to send it to both CSIR and TWAS
Check you will still be 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, and that you hold no residency visa for India or any developed country
Gather evidence of English proficiency if your medium of education was not English, plus evidence of your intent to return home afterwards
Confirm with your employer that you can hold the research assignment while on fellowship, since other assignments are prohibited
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a CSIR acceptance letter, or with one dated in a previous year - both are fatal
Exceeding the age limit on 31 December of the application year
Holding any residency visa for India or a developed country, which disqualifies outright
Not being currently employed with a research assignment in the home country
Applying for a second TWAS or OWSD programme in the same calendar year, which is not permitted
For sandwich applicants, failing to send the Registration and No Objection Certificate to both CSIR and TWAS rather than just one
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accompanying family members are entirely at your own expense, and the monthly stipend is not convertible into foreign currency, so any obligation in your home currency has to be met from other sources. TWAS publishes no stipend figure on this page.
document_audit: The acceptance letter must be the official letter from the host institution, in the sample format published on the TWAS page
The No Objection Certificate needs the Vice-Chancellor's or Registrar's signature - a departmental sign-off will not do
Evidence of intent to return home is a separate requirement and must be submitted with the application
Since the stipend is not convertible, keep banking arrangements for the fellowship period in mind early
alerts: The 2026 call is closed, with results expected at the end of 2026 or early 2027 and starts no earlier than 2027 - do not plan around an immediate departure
Only acceptance letters dated in the application year count, so an early letter obtained before the call opens can expire before you submit
You may apply for only one programme per calendar year across the TWAS and OWSD portfolio, and you forfeit TWAS Visiting Professor eligibility that year
The fellowship requires you to return to your home country on completion; it is a research placement, not a migration route
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure a CSIR host acceptance letter first, then register on the TWAS online portal, complete the form and upload documents, and (for sandwich applicants) send the No Objection Certificate to both CSIR and TWAS.
